trigger.trigger_note: ⚠️ CORRECTION 2026-08-24: the 're-fires per transition' claim below is EMPIRICALLY FALSE as deployed. See acceptance_delivery_broken_2026_08_24. The composite id advances in the read-action snapshot, but the deployed polling engine dedupes on the underlying request and never re-fires after the first (Pending) run, so acceptances must be filed by manual replay. The historical note is kept verbatim below because it is the evidence base for the (now-disproven) swap rationale. ||| Polling trigger, one run per STAGE CHANGE (dedupe id is <project_request_id>_<lead_stage_modified_on>, so it re-fires per transition — verified by the 2026-08-07 decline experiment and the 2026-08-18 Yanolja acceptance). Swapped from new_project_request 2026-08-18 after that request proved the old trigger fires exactly once per request, at Pending, while identity is still sentinel-withheld — so an acceptance could never be filed automatically (3/3 requests skipped, 0 re-fires across 3 later stage changes). A request's creation is its first stage event, so new Pending requests still produce a run (which the code skips at the stage gate). CUTOVER COMPLETE 2026-08-18T12:14Z via the documented out-of-band publish with --trigger (version 01a014cb-165c-…, verified triggers[0] active on updated_project_request). Note the RACE that preceded it: the PR #113 pipeline run was approved while the first out-of-band publish (01a014c9-0dd7-…, new trigger) was in flight, and published 01a014c9-815d-… thirty seconds later carrying the OLD new_project_request trigger forward (the pipeline reads the deployed version's trigger, by design). Both are superseded; if a trigger swap ever happens again, let the pipeline run finish FIRST, then do the --trigger publish.

tables.01KYV1R8BWAZ697HQ8P1QV80AF: SPOT Project Requests — request id -> the Notion Deal/Contact/Company page ids it produced, plus the raw payload. Owned by this Zap; the dedupe key that makes a retry or re-poll a no-op. 'Created On' is a Text field, not Date & Time, because Tables coerces a bare YYYY-MM-DD into the account timezone and stores the previous day.

partner_app.note: Solution Partner Operations Tool (SPOT; private, invite-only). Sibling triggers referral_lead_status_change (used by zapier-partner-lead-status-to-notion) and new_project_request (this Zap's ORIGINAL trigger, abandoned 2026-08-18 — it fires once per request at Pending, before identity is revealed, and never again; see stage_change_trigger). Also exposes a find_project_request SEARCH action: filter by id or email, or leave both blank to return every project request. That call is the cheapest way to see the account's real state and answered why this Zap sat at zero runs.

description: Zapier Solution Partner project request ACCEPTED (stage-change trigger, gated to Accepted — Pending arrives identity-withheld, Declined/Expired are deliberately not filed) -> upsert a Notion Contact, Company and Deal. Company resolves via the companies mirror Table by domain, then the contact's existing Related Company, then a live Notion query by Website, then create. An existing Contact is only filled in, never overwritten. The Deal opens at Lead from the Deals default template; Type, Value and Expected Close are left for whoever scopes it, and Status is never written on an existing Deal so a human's Declined cannot be undone. Raw payload preserved on the Deal page, in the request Table and in the run output.
durable_version_note: Pinned to 0.10.1, matching both sibling partner Zaps. A publish on 0.11.0 failed at run time with 'Dependency installation failed' — the durable runtime's pnpm enforces a 24-hour minimum release age. The same guard applies to @zapier/zapier-sdk and zod; check a version's publish date before bumping any of the three. FLAG NAMING (2026-08-07, CLI 0.71.1): publishing with `--zapier_durable_version` emits 'DEPRECATION WARNING - `zapier_durable_version` is deprecated and may be removed in a future release'. That is a RENAME, not a removal of version pinning — the canonical CLI flag is kebab-case `--zapier-durable-version` (likewise `--app-versions`), and the MCP publish tool takes camelCase `zapierDurableVersion`. Use those spellings and the warning goes away. The vendored workflow skills documented the snake_case forms until 2026-08-07, which is why a publish here went out with a deprecated flag; `npx skills update` on the bundle moved them to sdk_cli_min 0.67.4 / sdk_cli_validated 0.67.5 and the kebab-case spellings.

first_run.outcome: skipped — 'payload carried no usable email address'. operations: [] — NO steps ran, so nothing was written to Notion and no dedupe row exists. The request therefore remains unfiled and available to a later stage-change run.
first_run.latency: Request created 16:26:47.423, run created 16:27:44.773 — the polling trigger picked it up inside a minute. The claim was correct all along; there had simply been nothing to deliver.
what_it_proved: SPOT withholds identity with PROSE, not empty fields: email/first_name/last_name each carried 'Please accept or secure the lead to see the ...'. The run skipped only because that email sentence fails EMAIL_RE. The name sentences are non-empty strings that firstString accepted — they would have become the Contact and Deal titles had the address ever parsed. Fixed by SENTINEL_RE / firstRealString.
Four candidate lists missed: country <- `location` (which holds a REGION), apps <- `tool_requested`, servicesNeeded <- `service_requested`, stage <- `lead_stage`. All four now read.

Value vocabularies differ from Notion's: company_size '1-10' (Notion has 1-49/50-249/...), industry 'Retail & Wholesale' (Notion has 'Retail'), location 'Oceania (Australia & New Zealand)' (a region, not a country). All three were silently dropped by the guards — correct behaviour, but three empty fields. Now mapped; the country falls back to the website ccTLD when the region names more than one country.

This request came from `source: "Zapier Sales"` with `type: "match"` — an internal sales referral competing against other partners, NOT a directory lead. The PartnerPage-derived candidate spellings are therefore still worth keeping for a directory-sourced request.

acceptance_delivery_broken_2026_08_24.finding: The 2026-08-18 trigger swap (new_project_request -> updated_project_request) did NOT fix the 'fires once, at Pending' problem. The updated_project_request polling trigger, as deployed, fires exactly once per request — at the first poll (stage Pending) — and does NOT fire on later stage changes, even though the record's composite id (<request_id>_<lead_stage_modified_on>) advances. So acceptances never reach the workflow automatically; they must be filed by manual replay (see README manual-replay runbook).
acceptance_delivery_broken_2026_08_24.why_the_swap_looked_right_but_was_not: The swap rationale rested on (a) running updated_project_request as a READ ACTION and seeing the composite id advance on a stage change, and (b) the Yanolja acceptance. But (a) is a snapshot of current state, not the poll dedup engine's behaviour, and (b) was a MANUAL REPLAY, not a trigger-fired run. No trigger-fired acceptance run has ever occurred.
evidence: BMC Tooling 02700000000003u00hE: Pending run 01a03390 at 2026-08-24T11:38Z; declined 11:41Z; NO run for the Declined transition. A poll demonstrably ran at 19:28Z (it produced Commercial Laundry's Pending run) — 8h after the decline — and still did not fire BMC's advanced composite id. Rules out poll latency: the request is treated as already-seen.
Commercial Laundry 02700000000003A00hE: Pending run 01a0353e at 2026-08-24T19:28Z; accepted 23:06:50Z; NO run 45+ min later. Filed by manual replay at 23:53Z.

The live updated_project_request read-action poll returns all 5 requests with their CURRENT composite ids (including the changed ones), confirming the app surfaces the advance — but the deployed durable poller does not fire on it.
acceptance_delivery_broken_2026_08_24.root_cause_location: Zapier/SPOT side (the app trigger's dedup, or the durable polling engine). NOT fixable in workflow.ts — the durable is correct and files as designed when handed an accepted payload. A real fix needs a different delivery mechanism (e.g. a scheduled reconciliation sweep over find_project_request that files any Accepted-but-unfiled request, or a serializing classic-Zap front door).
acceptance_delivery_broken_2026_08_24.decision: Dennis, 2026-08-24: document the workaround now (this block + README), design/build the real fix separately. SPOT app 1.5.1 now exists; whether it changes this trigger's dedup is UNTESTED and worth checking when the fix is scoped.
acceptance_delivery_broken_2026_08_24.pin_1_5_1_attempt: 2026-08-25: pinned the trigger 1.5.0 -> 1.5.1 (out-of-band --trigger publish, version 01a03649-c796-7f94-acf5-e1e5097d4ead; enabled + triggers[0] active on updated_project_request confirmed) as a speculative fix, since 1.5.1's dedup behaviour cannot be inspected via MCP/CLI and the bug cannot be exercised without a real stage transition (a read/test-trigger only returns a snapshot; there is no write action to change a request's stage, and declining a live lead is off the table). So this is 'install and observe on the next real Pending->Accepted'. A Zapier support ticket was filed in parallel to get a definitive answer. RESULT: 1.5.1 does NOT fix it — see zapier_support_confirmation_2026_08_26. The trigger stays on 1.5.1 (latest, harmless) but the real fix is the reconciliation sweep.
acceptance_delivery_broken_2026_08_24.zapier_support_confirmation_2026_08_26: Zapier Product Escalations (Brittney/Brit C, ticket 9NPEKP-739EJ) pulled the deduplication logs for this workflow's trigger subscription and CONFIRMED the diagnosis: the poller dedupes on project_request_id, not the composite id. Cause: the updated_project_request trigger's output-field config marks project_request_id as the PRIMARY key, and on Zapier's platform a primary output field OVERRIDES the root-level id as the dedupe key — so the composite id is delivered in the payload but never consulted for dedup, and a request can only fire once, at first sighting. Same behaviour for classic and next-gen workflows (not a workflow-type difference). 1.5.1: the 1.5.1 test subscription shows the SAME dedupe field in the logs and 1.5.1's changes do not touch this trigger, so it does not fix it. Ownership: SPOT is Zapier-maintained; the fix sits on Zapier's side; escalated to the team that owns the integration, NO timeline given. Recommended workaround (Zapier's own): manual replay, or a scheduled reconciliation sweep against find_project_request. CUTOVER NOTE for when a fixed version ships: pin to it and toggle the workflow off then on so it starts a FRESH dedupe table; stage changes from BEFORE the fix will NOT fire retroactively (the first poll of a new subscription seeds the dedupe table without triggering); manual read/test bypasses dedup entirely, which is why read tests always showed the advanced ids.
acceptance_delivery_broken_2026_08_24.zapier_fix_shipped_2026_08_26: RESOLVED by Zapier. Brit C (ticket 9NPEKP-739EJ) confirmed the dedup fix was 'merged and approved', and SPOT app version 1.5.2 appeared (it did not exist during the investigation). Almost certainly the fix ships in 1.5.2 (the bug was in the trigger's output-field/dedupe-key config, which is version-gated). ACTION: re-pinned this trigger 1.5.1 -> 1.5.2 by editing trigger.selected_api and letting the merge pipeline republish (the pipeline compares declared vs deployed trigger and publishes the declared one when different — the sanctioned way to change a trigger; no out-of-band publish needed). STILL UNVERIFIED on our deployment: whether 1.5.2 actually fires on a real Pending->Accepted can only be confirmed by the next real acceptance (same testability limit). Per Zapier's cutover note, after the re-pin the workflow should be toggled off->on to reset the polling dedupe table (done post-merge). The spot-accepted-sweep-to-notion backstop STAYS ENABLED until a real acceptance is observed to fire this trigger; only then retire the sweep. If it does not fire, 1.5.2 didn't fix it and the sweep remains the mechanism.

stage_change_trigger.status: CLAIMED by this workflow as of the 2026-08-18 trigger swap (see trigger above). This block predates the swap; kept because its observations are the evidence base. The two-workflow split it anticipated (two-trigger-design.md) was superseded by the swap + an Accepted-only stage gate in this workflow.
stage_change_trigger.observed: 2026-08-07T00:49:43, when request 02700000000002800hE was declined in the portal as a deliberate test.
stage_change_trigger.delivers: The FULL record — every field new_project_request sends — plus `lead_stage_modified_on`. Not a delta.
stage_change_trigger.id_is_composite: `id` is `<project_request_id>_<lead_stage_modified_on>`, e.g. 02700000000002800hE_2026-08-07T00:49:43, and it ADVANCED with the stage change (was ..._2026-08-06T16:26:47 at Pending). Same shape referral_lead_status_change uses. A polling trigger dedupes on `id`, so a new id is a new item is a run — which is the evidence that this trigger fires per transition.
stage_change_trigger.WARNING_extractRequest: RESOLVED by the 2026-08-18 swap: on updated_project_request `r.id` is the COMPOSITE <request id>_<timestamp>, so keying dedupe on it would mint a duplicate Deal per stage change. extractRequest now reads `project_request_id` FIRST and only falls back to `r.id` with its `_` suffix stripped.
stage_change_trigger.declining_reveals_nothing: After Declined, email/first_name/last_name were STILL the sentinel sentences — consistent with 'accept or secure the lead'. So a Declined transition carries nothing to build a Contact from.
stage_change_trigger.record_survives_decline: find_project_request still returns the declined record, so declined requests stay queryable and win-rate data is available from the API rather than only from email.
stage_change_trigger.policy: DECIDED (Dennis, 2026-08-07): a declined or expired request creates NOTHING in the CRM — the records would be largely useless. A Table row is still written so the decline is countable.
stage_change_trigger.new_project_request_did_not_refire: Workflow runs stayed at 1 across the decline. Correct: the record changed but was not created. This is the gap the second workflow exists to close.

publish_caveats.open_draft_409: Verified against CLI 0.73.0: publish-workflow-version is rejected with a 409 while ANY draft is open on that workflow, because publishing the draft later would ship its stale content over the new version. `--ignore-open-drafts` overrides it, but that ships past work someone staged — prefer `list-workflow-drafts` to find the draft and `discard-workflow-draft` to clear it. Relevant here because two-trigger-design.md parks workflow B as a long-lived draft; the hazard is a forgotten draft on THIS workflow, whose next publish would then fail with a 409 unrelated to the change being made.
publish_caveats.flag_spelling: Kebab-case: --zapier-durable-version, --app-versions. The snake_case forms still work but emit a deprecation warning; the deprecation is on the ALIAS only. Verified against CLI 0.73.0 --help: --zapier-durable-version is live, fully documented, no replacement. Keep passing it — it 'defaults to server-configured version if omitted', and letting Zapier pick is what the 0.10.1 pin exists to prevent.
publish_caveats.newer_flags_unused: CLI 0.73.0 also exposes --disabled (cleaner than --enabled false) and --manual (triggerless on-demand workflow versions). Neither is used by this Zap; noted so a future publish does not rediscover them.
